title: 2 Moves vs 1 Move Against Stockfish
summary: On a viewer-made engine site, Tony gets two moves for every one Stockfish move. It is a king-capture variant (check doesn't end anything; you win by taking the king). He repeatedly sets up Qf3+Qxf7 double threats and takes Stockfish's king (~6:15). He then flips to Black with Stockfish getting 2 moves vs his 3; he loses once to a blunder (Bb5, Bxe8, 'White wins' ~7:53) and wins the rematch (~8:50).
rules: Turn order cycles: player moves twice, engine moves once (game 1).
King-capture variant: there is no check legality; the game ends when a king is captured ('the programmer made this a king capture variant').
Bonus games: player as Black, Stockfish (White) gets 2 moves, player gets 3.
